What is the name of the Swami whom autobiography impressed you so much?
questions.s: Replace 'whom' with 'whose'. 'Whom' is an object pronoun that refers to the person who was the recipient of an action. 'Whose' is a possessive pronoun that refers to the person to whom something belongs. Here, we need a possessive pronoun that refers to the Swami.

questions.q: Q3. Q3. He is among those rare individuals who not only dedicates himself but also inspire others to excel.

questions.q:
The team began searching for reasons for their poor performance in the tournament.

(CHSL 11/7/2019 S1)
questions.s:
The erroneous part of the sentence is "for their poor performance".

"The team" is a collective noun and is considered singular. Therefore, the possessive pronoun used should be "its", not "their".

"Their" is used for plural subjects, but here "team" is singular.

Correct sentence: The team began searching for reasons for its poor performance in the tournament.

questions.q: One (1)/ should keep (2)/ his word. (3)/ No Error (4)

When the subject is “One”, the corresponding pronoun must be “one’s”, not “his.”
So the correct sentence is: “One should keep one’s word.”

questions.q: These books are Sanju's (a) / and your then (b) / why Alok wanted (c) / to take them. (d) / No error (d)
questions.s:
After your, a noun must follow, or to show possession like Sanju’s, we use yours.
Correct sentence: These books are Sanju’s and yours; then why did Alok want to take them?

questions.q: Q10. He prostrated before (a)/ his master (b)/ who had returned from (c)/ London after a year.(d)
questions.s: The verb 'prostrate' is a transitive verb that requires a reflexive pronoun object when the action is done to oneself. Use 'prostrated himself'.

questions.q: Either of the apartments in this building is available for rent.

questions.s:
The correct answer is (b) they reconciled.
